method: OPEN AND QUOTED, from the RCH Melbourne Clinical Practice Guideline 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), retrieved 2026-09-23. Every pass claim is machine re-checkable. LICENCE: Free to read but NOT openly licensed -- each page carries '(c) 2026 The Royal Children's Hospital'. Quoted with attribution on the same footing as the 14 RCH guidelines and the Immunisation Handbook guidelines already in this compendium.

claims.claim: **These are for choosing initial empiric treatment.** Except where specified they **do not apply to neonates or immunocompromised patients**. **Always ask about previous antibiotic hypersensitivity.**
claims.source_text: These guidelines have been developed to assist doctors with their choice of initial empiric treatment … Except where specified, they do not apply to neonates or immunocompromised patients … Always ask about previous hypersensitivity reactions to antibiotic
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Change to narrow-spectrum agents once sensitivities are known.** Doses may need adjusting for neonates and for renal or hepatic impairment.
claims.source_text: Antibiotics should be changed to narrow spectrum agents once sensitivities are known … Dose adjustments may be necessary for neonates, and for children with renal or hepatic impairment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Durations are a guide**, and generally mean the **minimum total IV plus oral** course; stepping down from IV to oral is appropriate in many cases.
claims.source_text: Duration of treatment is given as a guide only and may vary with the clinical situation … 'Step down' from intravenous to oral treatment is appropriate in many cases … Durations given generally refer to the minimum total intravenous plus oral treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Ceftriaxone:** standard 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV daily; **severe infection — including meningitis, brain abscess and orbital cellulitis — 100 mg/kg (max 4 g) IV daily.**
claims.source_text: Ceftriaxone: standard dose 50 mg/kg (2 g) IV daily; severe infection (including meningitis, brain abscess and orbital cellulitis) 100 mg/kg (4 g) IV daily
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Cefotaxime:** 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV 12-hourly in week 1 of life, 6–8-hourly in weeks 2–4, 6-hourly after week 4.
claims.source_text: Cefotaxime: 50 mg/kg (2 g) IV 12H (week 1 of life), 6-8H (week 2-4 of life), 6H (>week 4 of life)
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Avoid ceftriaxone where possible in neonates under 41 weeks' gestation**, particularly if jaundiced or receiving calcium-containing solutions, including TPN.
claims.source_text: Where possible, ceftriaxone should be avoided in neonates <41 weeks gestation, particularly if jaundiced or receiving calcium containing solutions, including TPN
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Gentamicin, once daily:** birth–1 month 5 mg/kg IV daily; under 10 years 7.5 mg/kg (max 320 mg) IV daily; 10 years and over 6 mg/kg (max 560 mg) IV daily.
claims.source_text: Gentamicin Birth - 1 month: 5 mg/kg IV daily <10 years: 7.5 mg/kg (320 mg) IV daily ≥10 years: 6 mg/kg (560 mg) IV daily
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Gentamicin monitoring (normal renal function):** if more than 3 doses are needed, check the trough before the third dose and then every 3 days, **target under 1 mg/L**. In renal failure, check before every dose and discuss with a specialist.
claims.source_text: Normal renal function – if more than 3 doses required, the trough level (pre-dose) should be checked before the third dose and then every 3 days (target level <1 mg/L) … Renal failure – levels should be checked prior to each dose and the results should be discussed with a specialist familiar with therapeutic drug monitoring before the next dose is given
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Vancomycin trough targets:** 10–15 mg/L for cellulitis; 15–20 mg/L for severe infection (bacteraemia, endocarditis, pneumonia, osteomyelitis, meningitis) or a known high MIC.
claims.source_text: Target trough level 10–15 mg/L for cellulitis, 15-20 mg/L for severe infection (bacteraemia, endocarditis, pneumonia, osteomyelitis, meningitis) or known high MIC
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Penicillin allergy or MRSA risk:** substitute cefazolin or flucloxacillin with vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 750 mg) IV 6-hourly, **or** clindamycin 10 mg/kg (max 450 mg) oral tds, **or** trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 4/20 mg/kg (max 320/1600 mg) oral bd. **MRSA risk:** high-prevalence areas such as the NT and remote northern Queensland, prior MRSA, Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander or Pacific Islander child.
claims.source_text: If penicillin hypersensitivity or risk of MRSA: substitute Cefazolin or Flucloxacillin with Vancomycin 15 mg/kg (750 mg) IV 6H or Clindamycin 10 mg/kg (450 mg) oral tds or Trimethoprim with sulfamethoxazole (8/40 mg/mL) 4/20 mg/kg bd (320/1600 mg) oral bd … Residence in an area with high prevalence of MRSA, eg Northern Territory, remote communities in northern Queensland Previous colonisation or infection with MRSA (particularly recent) Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander or Pacific Islander child
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Meningitis over 2 months:** high-dose 3rd-generation cephalosporin. Duration: *S. pneumoniae* 10 days, *N. meningitidis* 5–7 days, Hib 7–10 days. **Consider dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg) IV 6-hourly for 4 days.**
claims.source_text: Meningitis Over 2 months of age S. pneumoniae5 N. meningitidis H. influenzae type b6 3rd gen cephalosporin (high dose)4 S. pneumoniae 10 days N. meningitidis 5–7 days H. influenzae type b 7–10 days Consider addition of Dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg (max 10 mg) IV 6H for 4 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Add vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 750 mg) IV 6-hourly if *S. pneumoniae* is suspected** (e.g. Gram-positive cocci on CSF). Stop it once cephalosporin sensitivity is confirmed or another cause is found.
claims.source_text: Over 2 months of age and possibility of penicillin-resistant pneumococci5 As above 3rd gen cephalosporin (high dose)4 and Vancomycin 15 mg/kg (750 mg) IV 6H … Vancomycin should be added if S. pneumoniae is suspected (eg Gram-positive cocci on CSF microscopy). This should be stopped if S. pneumoniae sensitivity to a third-generation cephalosporin is confirmed, as will be the case with most isolates, or once an alternative aetiology is confirmed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Meningitis under 2 months:** benzylpenicillin 60 mg/kg (max 2.4 g) IV — 12-hourly in week 1, 6-hourly in weeks 2–4, 4-hourly after week 4 — **plus** high-dose 3rd-generation cephalosporin. Gram-negative 3 weeks; GBS/Listeria 2–3 weeks.
claims.source_text: Benzylpenicillin 60 mg/kg (2.4 g) IV 12H (week 1 of life) 6H (week 2–4 of life) 4H (>week 4 of life) and 3rd gen cephalosporin (high dose)4 Gram-negative 3 weeks GBS/Listeria 2–3 weeks
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Encephalitis — aciclovir:** 500 mg/m² IV 8-hourly (3 months–12 years); 10 mg/kg IV 8-hourly (over 12 years); 3 weeks minimum.
claims.source_text: Aciclovir 20 mg/kg IV 12H (<30 weeks gestation), 8H (>30 weeks gestation to <3 months corrected age) 500 mg/m2 IV 8H (3 months – 12 years) 10 mg/kg IV 8H (>12 years) 3 weeks minimum
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Meningococcal contact prophylaxis:** ciprofloxacin 250 mg (5–12 years) or 500 mg (12 years and over) orally, single dose. If unable to take tablets, rifampicin 5 mg/kg (under 1 month) or 10 mg/kg (1 month and over) (max 600 mg) orally bd for 2 days.
claims.source_text: Ciprofloxacin 250 mg (5–12 years) 500 mg (≥12 years) oral single dose Unable to take tablets: Rifampicin 5 mg/kg ( <1 month) or 10 mg/kg (≥1 month) (max 600 mg) oral bd for 2 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Hib contact prophylaxis:** rifampicin 20 mg/kg (max 600 mg) orally daily for 4 days.
claims.source_text: H. influenzae type b Rifampicin 20 mg/kg (600 mg) oral daily 4 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Orbital (postseptal) cellulitis:** high-dose 3rd-generation cephalosporin IV, usually 3–4 days, then amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5 mg/kg (max 875 mg amoxicillin) orally bd; **10 days minimum in total.**
claims.source_text: Anaerobes 3rd gen cephalosporin (high dose)4 IV duration based on severity and improvement (usually 3-4 days) Switch to Amoxicillin/clavulanate (400/57 mg per 5 mL) 22.5 mg/kg (max 875 mg) (Amoxicillin component) = 0.3 mL/kg (max 11 mL) oral bd 10 days minimum total duration
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mild periorbital (preseptal) cellulitis:** cefalexin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) orally tds for 7–10 days. Bilateral, painless or non-tender swelling in a well child is more likely allergy.
claims.source_text: Mild Group A streptococci S. aureus H. influenzae spp. Cefalexin 20 mg/kg (750 mg) oral tds 7–10 days Bilateral findings and/or painless or non-tender swelling in a well looking child is more likely to be an allergic reaction
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Otitis media:** consider no antibiotics for 48 hours if over 6 months. If treating: amoxicillin 30 mg/kg (max 1 g) orally bd for 5 days.
claims.source_text: Otitis media Viruses S. pneumoniae M. catarrhalis H. influenzae spp. Group A streptococci Consider no antibiotics for 48 hours if over 6 months of age If treatment indicated Amoxicillin 30 mg/kg (1 g) oral bd 5 days
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pneumonia, mild (outpatient):** amoxicillin 30 mg/kg (max 1 g) orally tds for 3–5 days. **Moderate (inpatient):** the same for 5 days; consider benzylpenicillin 60 mg/kg (max 2.4 g) IV 6-hourly if unable to tolerate oral intake.
claims.source_text: Mild (outpatient) Viruses S. pneumoniae H. influenzae spp. Amoxicillin 30 mg/kg (1 g) oral tds 3-5 days Moderate (inpatient) As above Amoxicillin 30 mg/kg (1 g) oral tds 5 days Consider Benzylpenicillin 60 mg/kg (max 2.4 g) IV 6 H if unable to tolerate oral intake or vomiting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Severe pneumonia** (2 or more of: severe respiratory distress, severe hypoxaemia or cyanosis, marked tachycardia, altered mental state; or empyema needing ICU): 3rd-generation cephalosporin, 10 days minimum; consider azithromycin 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg) IV daily and oseltamivir.
claims.source_text: Severe (≥2 of: severe respiratory distress, severe hypoxaemia or cyanosis, marked tachycardia, altered mental state OR empyema ie requiring ICU care) As above plus S. aureus Group A streptococci Gram-negatives 3rd gen cephalosporin4 10 days minimum2 … Consider adding Azithromycin 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg) IV daily to cover M. pneumoniae and other atypical pathogens and Oseltamivir to cover influenza virus
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Tonsillitis — treat only features of GAS in a child 4 years or older AND a high-risk group or suppurative complications:** phenoxymethylpenicillin 250 mg bd (under 20 kg) or 500 mg bd (20 kg and over) orally for 10 days, **or** benzathine benzylpenicillin 450 mg IM (under 20 kg) / 900 mg IM (over 20 kg) once.
claims.source_text: Features of GAS infection in child ≥4 years AND high-risk group or suppurative complications: Phenoxymethylpenicillin (Penicillin V) 250 mg oral bd (<20 kg) 500 mg oral bd (≥20 kg) or Benzathine benzylpenicillin 450mg (600 000 units) IM (<20 kg), 900 mg (1.2 million units) IM (>20 kg) as a single dose 10 days oral treatment
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **High-risk groups for GAS:** Indigenous Australians · Māori and Pacific Islander · personal or family history of rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease · immunosuppressed.
claims.source_text: High-risk groups: Indigenous Australians Maori and Pacific Islander Personal history of rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease Family history of rheumatic fever or rheumatic heart disease Immunosuppressed
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Pertussis:** azithromycin 10 mg/kg (max 500 mg) daily from birth to 6 months; 10 mg/kg on day 1 then 5 mg/kg (max 250 mg) daily from 6 months; 5 days.

claims.claim: **Influenza — oseltamivir orally bd for 5 days:** 3 mg/kg (birth–12 months); 30 mg (over 12 months and under 15 kg); 45 mg (15–23 kg); 60 mg (23–40 kg); 75 mg (over 40 kg).

claims.claim: **Epiglottitis:** ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg (max 1 g) IV daily for 5 days.

claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **UTI over 3 months and not sick:** cefalexin 20 mg/kg (max 750 mg) orally tds, **or** trimethoprim 4 mg/kg (max 150 mg) orally bd, **or** trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 0.5 mL/kg (max 20 mL) orally bd; 5 days.
claims.source_text: Over 3 months of age and not sick E. coli P. mirabilis K. oxytoca Other Gram-negatives Cefalexin 20 mg/kg (750 mg) oral tds or Trimethoprim 4 mg/kg (150 mg) oral bd or Trimethoprim/Sulfamethoxazole (8/40 mg/mL) 0.5 mL/kg (20 mL) oral bd 5 days

claims.claim: **UTI under 3 months, sick, or acute pyelonephritis:** gentamicin (as above); 5–7 days for UTI, 7–10 days for pyelonephritis; consider early switch to cefalexin 25 mg/kg (max 1 g) qid under 12 months or 45 mg/kg (max 1.5 g) tds from 12 months.
claims.source_text: Under 3 months of age or sick or acute pyelonephritis Gentamicin Birth - 1 month: 5 mg/kg IV daily <10 years: 7.5 mg/kg (320 mg) IV daily ≥10 years: 6 mg/kg (560 mg) IV daily 5–7 days for UTI 7–10 days for pyelonephritis. Consider early switch to Cefalexin: <12 months: 25 mg/kg (max 1 g) oral qid ≥12 months: 45 mg/kg (max 1.5 g) oral tds

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Necrotising fasciitis:** vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 750 mg) IV 6-hourly **and** meropenem 20 mg/kg (max 1 g) IV 8-hourly **and** clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) IV 8-hourly; consider IVIg.

claims.claim: **Bites — established infection:** amoxicillin/clavulanate 22.5 mg/kg (max 875 mg amoxicillin) orally bd for 5 days. **Prophylaxis generally not required, except:** presentation after 8 hours · puncture wound that can't be debrided · hands, feet or face · deep tissue · open fracture · immunocompromised · cat bites. Check tetanus.
claims.source_text: Amoxicillin/Clavulanate (400/57 mg/5 mL) 22.5 mg/kg (875 mg) (Amoxicillin component) 0.3 mL/kg (11 mL) oral bd 5 days Treat established infection Prophylaxis generally not required, except: Presentation delayed >8 hours Puncture wound unable to be adequately debrided Bite on hands, feet, face Bite involves deep tissues (e.g. bones, joints, tendons) Bite involves an open fracture Immunocompromised patient Cat bites Check tetanus immunisation status
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sepsis over 2 months, CSF unknown (meningitis not excluded):** high-dose 3rd-generation cephalosporin; add vancomycin 15 mg/kg (max 750 mg) IV 6-hourly if a central line is in situ or MRSA is suspected.
claims.source_text: SEPSIS (OVER 2 MONTHS OF AGE) Sepsis with unknown CSF Meningitis not excluded S. pneumoniae5 N. meningitidis S. aureus Group A streptococci Gram-negatives 3rd gen cephalosporin (high dose)4 … If central line in situ (non-oncology) or suspected MRSA infection As above plus S. epidermidis Add Vancomycin 15 mg/kg (750 mg) IV 6H
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sepsis over 2 months with meningitis excluded:** cefazolin 50 mg/kg (max 2 g) IV 8-hourly **and** gentamicin.
claims.source_text: Sepsis with normal CSF Meningitis excluded: clinically (and LP therefore not performed) or normal CSF As above Cefazolin 50 mg/kg (2 g) IV 8H and Gentamicin
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Antimicrobial guidelines' (Last updated February 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Antimicrobial_guidelines/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Toxic shock syndrome:** high-dose 3rd-generation cephalosporin **and** vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV 6-hourly **and** clindamycin 15 mg/kg (max 600 mg) IV 8-hourly **and** IVIg 2 g/kg. GAS contact prophylaxis: cefalexin 25 mg/kg (max 1 g) orally bd for 10 days.
